column1: # price-table.tsv — consumer config for the --emit stage-economics arm (drift-kit/SPEC.md §The stage-economics meter).
# Columns are USD per single token (a $/MTok price / 1,000,000), tab-separated.
# One row per model id as it appears in a transcript's message.model.
# priced-as-of: 2026-08-29 — transcribed from the published Anthropic model-pricing
# table. Prices are a dated literal with no machine-readable feed to derive them from,
# so nothing but this date says when it was last checked; re-verify against the
# published table when kpi-price-table-age raises it. Every row below was re-verified
# against the published table on this date and every one was already correct.
# prices-valid-through: 2026-11-30 — and the field's meaning is weaker here than its
# wording, which is worth stating rather than leaving to be inferred. It normally names
# a known cliff. No future change is announced for any row, so this date is a RE-CHECK
# HORIZON: it says nobody has looked past it, not that a change lands on it.
# Both headers are read by kpi-price-table-age (drift-kit/SPEC.md §Bundled KPIs):
# age alone cannot see a cliff, since a freshly retyped table reads freshest on the
# morning its prices stop being true.
# cache_creation encodes the 1-HOUR cache-write price (2x base input). Sessions here
# run a 1h prompt-cache TTL; the 5-minute write (1.25x base input) applies only when
# a session drops to the short TTL, so a mixed-TTL corpus prices cache_creation high.
# Cache reads dominate the totals by one to two orders of magnitude, so the convention
# moves the result far less than the cache_read column does.
# RETRACTED CLIFF, recorded so nobody restores it from memory: the Sonnet 5 row was
# INTRODUCTORY pricing through 2026-08-31, scheduled to rise to 3 / 15 / 0.30 / 6 per
# MTok on 2026-09-01. The published table now states that 2 / 10 IS the standard price
# and that the increase WILL NOT OCCUR. So the 2.5x Opus:Sonnet ratio these rows carry
# does not step down, and a tier comparison run past 2026-08-31 is no longer overstating
# the saving — which is the opposite of what this block said until 2026-08-29.
# KNOWN UNDERCOUNT: fast mode bills the same model id at a different rate — Opus 5 at
# speed=fast is 10 / 50 per MTok, double the standard row below. The meter keys a price
# on the model id alone and cannot see the speed field, so any fast-mode turn prices at
# the standard rate and the reported cost is a floor. There is one row per model id by
# construction, so this is a stated limit rather than a second row.
